description: We are a team of curious innovators and space enthusiasts participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Through our theme, "Abandoned but not Forgotten," we aim to uncover the stories behind NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars, highlighting the scientific contributions, challenges, and human achievements represented by these forgotten remnants of space exploration.
summary:
We built Cosmic Horizon, an interactive 3D experience that turns humanity’s space exploration history into a digital museum. Instead of just reading about space, users can freely navigate between Earth, the Moon, and Mars.
​To address the challenge, we moved away from static, text-heavy documents and turned NASA's rich archives into a visual story. Visitors can spin 3D planetary models, scroll through historical timelines, and click on glowing orbital paths to uncover the data and stories behind past missions and the artifacts we've left on other worlds.
​This project matters because space exploration belongs to everyone, yet raw scientific data can feel intimidating. Cosmic Horizon bridges that gap. By making our cosmic heritage visually stunning and intuitive to explore, we hope to spark curiosity, preserve our greatest milestones, and inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts.
details:
Cosmic Horizon

Cosmic Horizon is an interactive 3D web platform that serves as a digital museum for humanity’s space exploration. Powered by verified NASA archival data, the site lets users navigate between Earth, the Moon, and Mars through a sleek, dark-themed interface. Visitors can freely rotate 3D planetary models, scroll through historical timelines, and click on glowing orbital paths to instantly uncover the stories and data behind past missions and human-made artifacts.

Built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebGL (Three.js), Cosmic Horizon gamifies the learning experience. It transforms dense aerospace data into an accessible, cinematic journey, making our cosmic heritage visually striking and easy to explore for everyone
